Package com.phasmidsoftware.visitor.java

Class Traversals

java.lang.Object
com.phasmidsoftware.visitor.java.Traversals
public final class Traversals extends Object
The Java entry points to Visitor's traversal engine.

Visitor's Scala API is driven by type classes supplied implicitly. This façade takes the two that matter — NeighbourFunction and Evaluator — as ordinary arguments, so a Java caller supplies them as lambdas or method references and needs to know nothing about Scala given instances: 


 Map<String, List<String>> graph = Map.of(
         "A", List.of("B", "C"),
         "B", List.of("D"),
         "C", List.of("D"),
         "D", List.of());

 TraversalResult<String, String> r =
         Traversals.bfs("A", v -> graph.getOrDefault(v, List.of()));

 r.visited();   // [A, B, C, D]
 r.cameFrom();  // {B=A, C=A, D=B}

Each traversal comes in four forms: with and without an early-termination goal, and with or without an Evaluator. The plain forms evaluate each node to itself, so TraversalResult.results() equals TraversalResult.visited(); the ...Evaluating forms let the evaluator transform and filter.

A goal predicate halts the traversal after recording the first node it accepts. That node is present in the result; nothing beyond it is visited.

Every method is a static method on a final class that cannot be instantiated.

    • traverseTree

      public static <H, V> TraversalResult<V,V> traverseTree(H root, NeighbourFunction<H,V> rootChildren, NeighbourFunction<V,V> children, Order order)
      Depth-first traversal of a tree whose root may have a different type from its descendants.

      The root itself is not visited: rootChildren yields the nodes the traversal begins from, and children carries it down from there.

      Where the root is of the same type as its descendants, use dfs instead: it records the start node. You can pass the same function twice here, but the root will then be absent from the result, which is rarely what is wanted. This entry point is for a root that is not itself a node — a tree object whose children are strings, say — where there is nothing of type V to record for it. Given a homogeneous adjacency, dfs returns exactly this result with the root included: first in Order.PRE, last in Order.POST. See issue #30.

      TraversalResult.cameFrom() is always empty for a tree traversal, because the engine does not record came-from where the parent is already evident from the tree's shape.

      Type Parameters:
      H - the root type
      V - the node type
      Parameters:
      root - the root structure
      rootChildren - the children of the root
      children - the children of each node below the root
      order - whether a node is recorded before or after its descendants
      Returns:
      the nodes in depth-first order
